target_moa.text: Voxelotor is a hemoglobin S (HbS) polymerization inhibitor that binds with 1:1 stoichiometry to the N-terminal alpha chain of hemoglobin, increases hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, and thereby inhibits HbS polymerization, decreasing hemolysis.

citations.quote: Voxelotor (GBT440, OXBRYTA), a new molecular entity (NME), is an orally administered, hemoglobin S (Hgb S) polymerization inhibitor which binds with 1:1 stoichiometry and exhibits preferential partitioning to red blood cells (RBCs). By increasing the affinity of Hb for oxygen, voxelotor demonstrates dose-dependent inhibition of HbS polymerization.
Mechanism of Action	Voxelotor inhibits the polymerization of sickle cell hemoglobin, increases hemoglobin affinity to oxygen, and improves RBC deformability, thereby decreasing hemolysis.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were headache (26% vs 22% placebo), diarrhea (20% vs 10%), abdominal pain (19% vs 13%), nausea (17% vs 10%), fatigue (14% vs 10%), rash (14% vs 10%), and pyrexia (12% vs 7%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 3% (3/88) of patients (headache, drug hypersensitivity, pulmonary embolism, 1 each).
